H4-AC5 IS judgment="true". NO VERDICT IS OFFERED HERE; the reading itself lives in
CG-s-39.what-republished-the-projection.result.md s.6 @55f55e7cca and is reproduced in
outline below so the grader can find it without opening a second file.

(1) CAN A COUNT ON THIS PLANE BE CITED TODAY, AND UNDER WHAT CONDITION?
Yes, but only as an instantaneous reading carrying its vintage AND its manifest id, and only
for a family whose parent class is stable. A count parented to S3_BUCKET_POLICY is a reading
of a value that changes whenever anybody writes an object to the corresponding bucket -- no
derive, no deploy, no schedule involved. Three such counts fell to zero in nine hours today
with every producer input unmoved. CONDITION: cite the number with <vintage> / <manifest_id>
and do not carry it across any interval in which an S3 write could have occurred, which is
every interval.

(2) CAN THE DEFERRED F11-AC3 SERVED RE-TAKE BE MADE READABLE BY ANYTHING SHORT OF AN
ATTRIBUTION? It already is, now that the attribution exists, and it would NOT have been
without one. The discriminator is not the count: it is the pair (nodes_snapshot_id,
edges_snapshot_id) plus edges_skipped_missing_endpoint in the served build's own manifest,
together with the worker's INCR_NODE_DELTA / INCR_EDGE_DELTA lines. A drop caused by THIS
mechanism shows an UNMOVED edges snapshot, a MOVED nodes snapshot, and a rise in
edges_skipped_missing_endpoint EQUAL to the edge fall. A fix that never reached the plane
shows none of that. So the re-take is readable if and only if it reads the manifest beside
the count; read on its own the count is still ambiguous and no attribution repairs that.

(3) EXPLAIN THE REPUBLISH, OR RE-PARENT? Re-parent. The explanation is done and helps nobody:
every component behaved correctly. The Lambda upserted a bucket node because a bucket was
written to; the worker rebuilt because the branch head advanced; the refresh deleted edges
whose endpoint no longer existed. Nothing here is a bug that can be switched off, and the
standing moratorium correctly forbids standing up a monitor. THE DEFECT IS THE PARENT CHOICE,
and the controlled comparison is inside the same graph in the same window: OWNED_BY
S3Key -> S3_BUCKET sat at 232 and S3Key at 381 while the policy-parented family lost 124.
QUALIFIER THAT CHANGES WHO MUST ACT: re-parenting fixes the BLAST RADIUS, not the collision
that fires the gun -- a Lambda writing node_id = <bare bucket name> into a table where that
string is another class's canonical key. After a re-parent the same overwrite still destroys
an S3_BUCKET_POLICY node on every S3 write; it just stops taking a boundary-edge family with
it. Whether that residue is acceptable is a decision above this cell, stated here so nobody
reads a deployed re-parent as a closed key-space problem.

determinism.method: SPLIT, BECAUSE THE FOUR ARMS ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF QUANTITY AND CALLING THEM ALL 'STABLE' WOULD HIDE THE INTERESTING PART. H4-AC1, H4-AC2 and H4-AC4 were each run TWICE against the same inputs (once while developing, once captured verbatim to h4_ac1_run.txt / h4_ac2_run.txt / h4_ac4_run.txt) and the deciding lines compared. H4-AC3 is a LIVE READ of a plane this very cell has just proved is event-driven and therefore MUST be allowed to move: re-running it is not a determinism test, it is a fifth point. Its stability claim is made instead on the two CONTROLS inside the single run -- the positive and the negative -- plus the vintage and manifest id printed beside every count, which is what makes the reading re-checkable by anybody at that vintage.
